explanation: An ecosystem consists of biotic communities interacting with their abiotic (nonliving) environment. The abiotic components include the atmosphere, water, and soil. The biotic components are living organisms categorized by their food source: 1) Autotrophs (Producers) generate food for the ecosystem using only inorganic nutrients and an outside energy source. They include photoautotrophs (such as land plants and algae) and chemoautotrophs (some bacteria). 2) Heterotrophs (Consumers) consume organic food generated by autotrophs. Consumers include herbivores, carnivores, omnivores, detritivores, and decomposers.

questions.q: What are autotrophs and what do they require to produce organic nutrients?
opts: They are decomposers that require organic waste and water.
They are producers that require only inorganic nutrients and an outside energy source.
They are consumers that require organic matter generated by other animals.
They are parasites that require a host organism to survive.
questions.exp: The notes state that Autotrophs (Producers) 'Require only inorganic nutrients and an outside energy source to produce organic nutrients.'

questions.q: Which of the following is categorized as a heterotroph in an ecosystem?
questions.exp: The notes list 'Herbivores, Carnivores, Omnivores, Detritivores, Decomposers' as types of Heterotrophs (Consumers).
